A question every parent asks

Why should I entrust my child to you?

More than chess.

A disciplined environment for developing better thinkers.

At an early age, children are constantly learning how to make decisions, respond to mistakes, manage pressure and think independently.

Chess gives us a remarkable environment in which to practise those abilities deliberately.

My role is not simply to teach your child how the pieces move.

It is to challenge their thinking, refine their decision-making and help them become more deliberate in how they approach problems.

Joseph Gathogo, FIDE School Instructor
The approach

Chess taught as a way of thinking.

Every student begins with a private assessment. From there, each lesson is built around their own games, their temperament and their goals.

The result is a young player who sits with a hard problem, weighs every option, and carries that discipline into the classroom and beyond.

Focus

Staying with one problem until it is solved, without reaching for a screen.

Judgement

Weighing options and consequences before acting, on the board and off it.

Resilience

Losing a game, understanding why, and returning stronger.

Composure

Competing calmly under pressure, and speaking up with confidence.

Joseph's recommendation

Online sessions are KES 1,000 on every programme.

Why most families who are serious choose Gold
  • Habits are built daily. A lesson once a week is easy to forget. Daily training turns good thinking into instinct.
  • Nothing extra to buy. Books, courses, videos and the full training system are included. On Standard they are bought separately; on Silver at half price.
  • Real opponents, real pressure. One-to-one games against other strong players and frequent tournament simulations, so a real tournament feels familiar, not frightening.
  • A coach in their corner. Joseph attends tournaments with your child anywhere in Nairobi, arranges entries, prepares them beforehand and analyses every game afterwards.
  • Only KES 1,000 more per session than Standard, for all of the above.
